attributes.title: Level 2

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you change the sprite kinds in the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which sprite kind should be changed to make something happen when the the Projectile overlaps with the Food sprite?


Solution: 

In the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block, the Player sprite kind should be replaced with the Projectile sprite kind so that the code is triggered when a Projectile sprite overlaps with a Food sprite.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, nothing happens when the Projectile overlaps with the moving banana sprites. 


Fix the bugs in the code so that the banana is destroyed and a special effect happens when the Projectile overlaps with it.

subgroups.title: Debugging Projectiles

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓Did you change the sprite name in the [set sprite to projectile from sprite] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Which sprite should be sending the Projectile?

❓How else might the Projectile be used in this game?


Solution:

The sprite in the [set sprite to projectile from sprite] block should be changed from banana to monkey.

﻿
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the Projectile is sent from the bananas, and destroys them immediately.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the Projectiles are sent from the correct sprite.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Did you change the sprite name in the [destroy sprite] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Does the [destroy sprite] block have the correct sprite name selected?


❓ Why is it helpful to use the otherSprite bubble rather than calling a specific sprite in this [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block?


Solution:

The otherSprite bubble from the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block needs to be dragged into the sprite name slot of the [destroy sprite] block. This causes any Food sprite kinds to be destroyed when the hero overlaps with them, not just specific sprites.
steps.instructions:
When a projectile is sent from the monkey sprite, there is an error!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the Projectile destroys any banana sprite that it overlaps with.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 2 of Yellow Belt! In this level, you’ll learn about loops, which are chunks of code that repeat a sequence of instructions. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 2:

badges.title: Around and Around
badges.description: Use loops to repeat code in a project.

badges.title: The Times, They Are A-Changin’
badges.description: Use a game update loop to repeat actions in a project.

badges.title: Bouncing off the Walls
badges.description: Set a sprite to bounce on walls in a project.

badges.title: Pew Pew
badges.description: Launch a projectile from a specific sprite.

badges.title: Button Masher
badges.description: Use an event triggered by the A button in a project.

badges.title: I Like to Move It Move It
badges.description: Use velocity to make a sprite move on its own.
